assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Hyundai Motor India (consolidated, Rs crore; subsidiaries are tiny: an engineering-services company and an insurance broker). Revenue = vehicles sold (domestic + exports, company wholesale basis) x revenue per vehicle (all operating revenue incl. parts, engineering services, export incentives and government scheme income, divided by vehicles). The domestic / export build is in `build` and is checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/HYUNDAI.ctx.js. FY26 base: 775,031 vehicles (584,906 domestic + 190,125 exports), revenue Rs70,763 cr, Rs913,033 per vehicle. Screener's Net Profit equals Profit for EPS (no minorities), so no patchRaw. Shares 81.25 cr (IPO in Oct-2024 was a pure offer for sale: no new shares). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS as the street does.

volume._why: Company wholesale volumes (domestic + exports). FY27E 827,673 (+6.8%): domestic +9% (guidance 8-10%; Apr-Aug +12.6% to 247,980; Sep-Mar must grow ~7% against the GST-boosted base, helped by the Bayon mid-SUV from Oct-2026, the localised compact EV in H2 and the Pune third shift from Oct-2026; management expects the industry to grow only in low single digits in H2) and exports flat at 190,125 (guidance 8-10%, but Apr-Aug was -11.7%: Q1 -19.6% on the West Asia conflict and the June supplier fire, July +31%, August -31% on shipping constraints). FY28E +9.9% (domestic +10%: full year of two new nameplates, Chennai Plant 1 utilisation 72% to ~90% in CY27, Pune Phase 2 by CY28; exports +10% from a low base: new Venue global sourcing, Exter LHD, Verna PE, EV and Bayon exports). FY29E +8% (both). Capacity 994k at Mar-26 (Chennai 824k + Pune 170k), 1.07 mn after Pune Phase 2 (CY28), >1.1 mn by 2030: FY29E volume is ~92% of the CY28 capacity. Brokers: MOSL ~9% volume CAGR FY26-28E; Nirmal Bang 9.3%; JM domestic 8.5%/8.2%, exports 10%/12%.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: Revenue per vehicle = revenue from operations / wholesale volume: Rs897,690 (FY24), Rs907,982 (FY25), Rs913,038 (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs917,251 (+0.8% YoY, +2.1% QoQ; JM). FY27E +2.5%: three price rises in CY26 (~100bp cumulative), lower discounts (2.8% of ASP in Q1FY27 vs 3.4%), Bayon (above Venue) and the EV (priced above ICE equivalents) in H2, rupee weakness on export ASPs (export ASP +7% YoY in Q1). FY28E +3%: full-year mix of two new SUVs and the EV. FY29E +2.5%: price ~1.5% plus mix. Parts revenue fell in FY26 (Rs3,392 cr vs Rs4,306 cr) and is a drag we do not try to forecast separately.
assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income): 12.5% FY23, 13.0% FY24, 12.9% FY25, 12.1% FY26, 9.3% in Q1FY27 (supplier fire cost ~13,900 vehicles, mostly Creta; exports -20%; commodity hit ~100bp QoQ and ~200bp YoY in precious metals and copper; Pune stabilisation costs; employee cost +20%). Guidance: 11-14% for FY27, reiterated on 30-Jul-2026. FY27E 11.0% = Q1 9.3% plus ~11.5% for Q2-Q4 (volume recovery, price rises, no launch discounts on new models) - the bottom of the range, because commodity pressure is not over and the EV and Bayon launches carry marketing and start-up costs. FY28E 12.3%: Chennai Plant 1 utilisation back to ~90%, operating leverage on the Pune plant, localisation 83% to 90% by 2030. FY29E 12.8%, still below FY24-25 (~13%): royalty (2.8% of revenue), EV mix and competition (M&M, Tata, Maruti, Kia in SUVs). Street FY27E 11.0% (Nirmal Bang) to 12.1% (BOB Caps); FY28E 11.4% to 13.3%; Nomura 11.5% / 12.7% / 13.4%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 capex guided at ~Rs7,500 cr, 'the highest ever' (Q4FY26 call, 8-May-2026): mainly Pune Phase 2 (170k to 250k by CY28) and Chennai upgrades, plus the two FY27 launches. The company plans to invest Rs45,000 cr over FY26-FY30 in capacity, electrification and 26 new products and variants (AR FY26); Screener capex FY26 Rs4,266 cr. Pune Phase 3 (+70k to ~320k by 2030) follows. We model Rs8,500 cr a year for FY28-29E; spending the full Rs45,000 cr plan would mean ~Rs11,000 cr a year in FY28-30, a downside risk to free cash flow.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs2,198 cr = 7.7% of average gross block (Rs28,692 cr), but gross block jumped by Rs7,997 cr when the Pune plant was capitalised in H2FY26. Q1FY27 depreciation Rs557 cr (Rs2,228 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs725 cr) and depreciates capex at once, although much of the Rs7,500-8,500 cr a year will sit in CWIP until Pune Phase 2 starts; 6.2% gives Rs2,259 cr in FY27E, Rs2,755 cr in FY28E and Rs3,282 cr in FY29E (3.4% of revenue vs 3.0-3.2% in FY24-26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury = cash and bank deposits (Rs10,552 cr at Mar-26) less borrowings (Rs1,098 cr incl. leases) = Rs9,461 cr. FY26 interest income Rs547 cr (fixed deposits Rs455 cr, tax refunds Rs14 cr, others Rs76 cr; AR FY26 consolidated note 30) on average gross cash of Rs9,566 cr = 5.7%; on average net cash (~Rs8,600 cr) ~6.4%. FY25: Rs616 cr. Deposit rates fell in 2025-26, so 5.8% on net treasury.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: royalty received Rs120 cr (FY26), rental income Rs49 cr, other non-operating income Rs92 cr and profit on asset sales Rs7 cr = ~Rs270 cr in FY26, growing with the business; plus a small allowance for exchange gains. FY26 reported other income Rs949 cr (AR note 30) = interest Rs547 cr + royalty Rs120 cr + exchange gain Rs133 cr + rental Rs49 cr + other Rs100 cr; Screener shows Rs986 cr (including Rs4 cr of exceptional items and classification differences). TTM to Jun-26 Rs1,001 cr. We do not forecast most exchange gains (Rs133 cr in FY26, Rs13 cr in FY25), so FY27E other income (~Rs800 cr) is below FY26.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (SIPCOT soft loan, leases, working-capital lines)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs106 cr; Q1FY27 Rs27 cr. Borrowings Rs1,098 cr at Mar-26 (long-term Rs455 cr, mainly the Tamil Nadu sales-tax soft loan; short-term Rs542 cr; leases Rs101 cr), repaid over time.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 25.9% in FY25 and FY26 (statutory 25.17% plus disallowances such as CSR); Q1FY27 26.0%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs21 a share for FY25 and FY26 (30% and 31.4% of EPS). The revised dividend policy (Oct-2025) sets no fixed payout. FY24 included ~Rs15,400 cr of dividends paid to HMC before the IPO (derived from the fall in reserves), which we do not expect to repeat while capex is Rs7,500-8,500 cr a year.

Revenue per vehicle is one blended figure; the split of revenue by geography (AR FY26 note 29: domestic vehicles Rs45,150 cr, exported vehicles Rs15,598 cr; parts Rs3,392 cr; services Rs5,251 cr; other operating revenue Rs1,372 cr) is shown in the report but not modelled separately. dcf._betaWhy: Net cash; cyclical but large, diversified PV maker with an export arm; cost of equity 11.9%.
dcf._tgWhy: India's nominal GDP grows ~10%; PV penetration is low (~30 cars per 1,000 people), but Hyundai is losing share and pays a royalty for its technology. 5.5%, the middle of the house 5-6% range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~10% to 8% over 15 years: volume ~4-5% plus price and mix.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: EBITDA margin held at ~12.5%, the middle of the 11-14% guidance band and the FY23-26 average.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex falls from ~9-10% of revenue (Pune, EVs, 26 launches) to 4%, close to depreciation; the FY23-FY26 average was 5.5%.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Bayon and the compact EV take Hyundai's domestic share back toward 14% (FY24 level), exports return to 8-10% growth as the West Asia route reopens and the new Venue becomes a global product, Pune Phase 2 arrives on time and margins return to ~13.5%, the FY24-25 level.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: The GST step-up fades into low single-digit industry growth; M&M, Tata, Maruti and Kia keep taking SUV share, so domestic volume grows ~4% a year; exports stay weak; commodity inflation persists and margins stay near FY27's 10-11%; the ₹45,000 cr capex plan is spent in full and depreciation rises faster.

cover.headline: A good car company at a fair price: the launches are coming, the premium is not
cover.lead: Hyundai Motor India is India's #4 car maker by domestic volume (12.6% share in FY26, down from 14.6% in FY24) and its largest exporter, 82.5% owned by Hyundai Motor Company, to which it pays a ~2.8% royalty. Volumes and margins are at a low: domestic sales fell two years running as M&M and Tata out-launched it, and a supplier fire and the West Asia conflict cut Q1FY27 EBITDA margin to 9.3% and profit by 35%. Two all-new SUVs (the Bayon mid-SUV and a localised EV), a third shift at Pune and an 8-10% volume guide point to recovery in H2. The street values the stock on **P/E on FY28E (24-30x, median 26x)**. We forecast EPS of ₹63.9 / ₹79.7 / ₹89.7 for FY27-29E, a little below the street. Applying the house rule (**25.5x Sep-28E EPS of ₹84.7**) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹1,662, DCF ₹1,459. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The recovery is real, but it starts from a low base
arguments.p: Domestic sales rose 23% in July and 24% in August (Apr-Aug +12.6%); production lost in June has been made up; Bayon bookings opened on 23-Sep. We model {{F.volume.0|num}} vehicles in FY27E (+{{as.volume.growth.0|n1}}%: domestic +9%, exports flat), then +10% and +8%. FY27E EPS of ₹63.9 is still below FY26's ₹66.9 and FY24's ₹74.6.

arguments.h: Share loss is the core problem, and two launches only start to fix it
arguments.p: Hyundai went from #2 to #4 in FY26 (M&M 660k, Tata 631k, Hyundai 585k). One mid-SUV and one EV will help, but rivals launch several SUVs a year and Kia, its sister company, competes in the same segments. Management targets an exit share above ~12.3%, not a return to 14-15%.

arguments.h: Margins: 11-14% guided, 9.3% in Q1; we model {{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} → {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}}
arguments.p: Commodities (precious metals, copper), the Pune ramp-up, weak exports and launch costs weigh on FY27. Utilisation at Chennai Plant 1 (72% → ~90% in CY27) and lower discounts help FY28. A 2.8% royalty to the parent and rising depreciation (₹45,000 cr capex plan to FY30) cap returns.

At ₹2,031 the stock trades at 25.5x our FY28E EPS and 33.3x trailing. Its forward P/E has a median of 28.4x over the last 12 months (we skip the first year after the Oct-2024 listing); auto peers sit 10.0% below their own medians for the same window. That gives 25.5x, close to the street's 24-30x. The street's higher targets (median ₹2,334) come mostly from higher FY28 earnings.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much of the June production loss and the margin shortfall came back; export run-rate.
Bayon launch and pricing (festive 2026) and the localised compact EV (H2FY27): booking and dispatch run-rates, PLI eligibility.
Festive retail (Oct-Nov 2026) against the GST-boosted base of Oct-Nov 2025; industry growth in H2 ("low single digits", management).
West Asia shipping: whether exports recover to 50k+ a quarter (Middle East orders, Exter LHD, new Venue in 35 markets).
Pune third shift (from Oct-2026), Pune Phase 2 (250k by CY28) and the FY28 capex plan; any change in royalty or dividend policy.

sections.title: One business, two markets: India (three-quarters of revenue) and exports to emerging markets

blocks.p: Hyundai Motor India (HMIL) makes and sells Hyundai passenger vehicles in India and exports them to emerging markets in the Middle East, Africa, Latin America and Asia. It sells 13-15 models: SUVs (Creta, Venue, Exter, Alcazar; 68% of FY26 domestic volume, 70% in Q1FY27), hatchbacks (Grand i10, i20) and sedans (Aura, Verna), plus the Creta Electric. It has three assembly plants: two in Chennai (824,000 a year) and Talegaon near Pune (170,000, bought from General Motors in 2023, producing the new Venue since Oct-2025). It also does engineering work for Hyundai Motor Company (HMC) and runs a small insurance-broking subsidiary.

Two features make it different from Maruti, Tata or M&M. **It is a subsidiary, not a group flagship**: HMC owns 82.5%, licenses the designs, engines and technology for a royalty (₹1,975 cr in FY26, 2.8% of revenue), and supplies parts through group companies. **It is an export hub**: 190,125 vehicles (25% of volume, 26% of revenue) went abroad in FY26, and HMC now sources the new Venue for some markets from India.

sections.title: Thirty years in India: from Santro to SUVs, a pre-IPO cash-out and India's largest IPO

blocks.p: HMC set up HMIL in 1996; its Chennai plant (1998) was HMC's first fully integrated plant outside South Korea, and the Santro made it India's #2 car maker by 1999, a position it held for over two decades with i10, i20, Verna and, from 2015, the Creta. It sold ~13.5 mn vehicles in India and abroad by 2026. The listing was a sale by the parent, not a fundraise: HMC took ~₹15,400 cr of dividends out in FY24 and then sold 17.5% in the Oct-2024 IPO for ₹27,859 cr.

sections.title: Indian car demand hit a record after GST 2.0, but SUVs and new launches take the growth

blocks.p: India sold 46,43,439 passenger vehicles in FY26 (+7.9%, SIAM wholesales), a record, with utility vehicles (SUVs and MPVs) at 67% of the market. The first half was weak; GST 2.0 (22-Sep-2025) cut the tax on small cars from 29-31% to 18% and on larger cars from 45-50% to a flat 40%, and demand jumped. The new fiscal year began strongly (April +25.4%; Q1FY27 ~12.7 lakh, +26%), but from October the industry laps the post-GST base. Hyundai's MD expects "lower single digit" growth in H2 and 6-9% for FY27.

blocks.p: Hyundai held India's #2 spot for most of two decades. In FY26 it slipped to #4: M&M sold 660,276 SUVs (+20%) and Tata 631,387 vehicles (+14%) while Hyundai sold 584,906 (−2.3%). Rivals launched more new SUVs and electric SUVs (Maruti's Victoris and e-Vitara among them), and Kia, Hyundai's sister company, competes with the Seltos and other models on shared group platforms. Hyundai's answer is the new Venue (Oct-2025), refreshed Exter and Verna, and two all-new nameplates in H2FY27.

sections.title: India: two years of lost share; Bayon, an EV and a third Pune shift to turn it

blocks.p: Hyundai sold 5,84,906 vehicles in India in FY26 (−2.3%) while the market grew 7.9%. H1FY26 was weak (Q1 −11.5%, Q2 −6.8%) as the market waited for the GST cut; H2 recovered (Q3 +0.4%, Q4 +8.5%, a record quarter). FY27 started well (April-May +13%) until a fire at a supplier cost ~13,900 vehicles of June production, mostly the Creta: Q1FY27 domestic was 1,39,374 (+5.4%). July (+23.3%) and August (+23.6%) made up most of the loss; Apr-Aug was 2,47,980, +12.6%.

What drives FY27-FY28: (1) the **Bayon** mid-SUV (named on 14-Sep-2026, bookings from 23-Sep; a 4.0-4.4 m "technology-first" SUV between the Venue and the Creta, launched for the festive season); (2) a **localised compact EV** in H2FY27, Hyundai's first mass-market EV, aiming for PLI incentives; (3) the **Pune third shift** from Oct-2026 (more Venue for India and export); and (4) lower discounts (2.8% of price in Q1FY27 vs 3.4%). Against that: the industry laps the post-GST base from October, and a reported production-plan increase for CY26 (to ~820,000 from ~770,000; Autocar Pro, 15-Sep-2026, not confirmed by the company) suggests management sees demand but also that inventory will be built ahead of the launches.

blocks.p: Exports were 1,90,125 vehicles in FY26 (+16.4%, against a 7-8% guide) and ₹15,598 cr of vehicle revenue (+21%), helped by a push into Central and South America and by the new Venue, which HMC now sources from India. Then the US-Iran conflict disrupted shipping to the Middle East, a key export region (Nirmal Bang calls the exposure 'meaningful'), from the end of FY26: Q1FY27 exports fell 19.6% to 38,708; July recovered to 21,150 (+31%, the highest in over 100 months) but August fell to 11,400 (−31%) on logistics. Apr-Aug exports were ~71,258, about −12%. Export prices are rising (ASP +7% YoY in Q1FY27) as the rupee weakens and the mix moves to SUVs (only 13-14% of exports are SUVs today, vs 70% at home).

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Hyundai India has real advantages (a global parent's technology, a respected brand, a lean cost base and an export network no Indian rival has) but no moat in its home market. FY25-FY26 proved it: when M&M and Tata out-launched it, Hyundai lost two points of share in two years and slipped to #4. Its margins (12-13%) are good for a mass-market carmaker but are not protected; they depend on launches, utilisation and the parent's product pipeline, and they are paid for with a permanent 2.8% royalty.

sections.title: Revenue up 73% since FY21, but profit peaked in FY24 and has fallen for two years

blocks.p: Hyundai India's revenue went from ₹40,972 cr in FY21, a Covid year, to ₹69,829 cr in FY24 (+19% a year) as chip supply returned, SUVs (Creta, Venue, then Exter) took over the range and exports grew. Then growth stopped: revenue was ₹69,193 cr in FY25 and ₹70,763 cr in FY26 (+2%), because domestic volumes fell two years running (614,721 → 598,666 → 584,906) while M&M, Tata and Maruti launched more SUVs. EBITDA margin peaked at 13.0% in FY24 and slid to 12.1% in FY26 and 9.3% in Q1FY27. Net profit peaked at ₹6,060 cr (EPS ₹74.6) in FY24 and fell to ₹5,432 cr (₹66.9) in FY26; the year to Jun-2026 was ₹4,950 cr (₹60.9).

sections.title: High returns on a lean balance sheet; capex now doubling and dividends to the parent first

blocks.p: Hyundai runs on negative working capital: suppliers are paid in ~52 days while inventory is ~26 days and customers pay in ~11, so dealers and suppliers fund the business. Over FY21-FY26 cash from operations was ₹38,043 cr, capex ₹18,928 cr and dividends ₹19,994 cr, of which ₹15,436 cr went out in FY24 (mostly to Hyundai Motor Company) before the IPO. Reported ROE of 30-42% in FY24-FY26 is inflated by that pre-IPO payout, which shrank equity to ₹10,666 cr at Mar-2024. On a normal balance sheet returns are still high (ROCE 38% in FY26 on Screener's basis), but they are falling as capex rises: ₹4,266 cr in FY26, ~₹7,500 cr guided for FY27, and a ₹45,000 cr plan to FY30 (Pune Phase 2 and 3, electrification, 26 launches).

With capex of ₹7,500-8,500 cr a year and a ~32% payout, we expect free cash flow near zero in FY27E and modest after that; net cash falls from ~₹9,500 cr to ~₹7,000-8,000 cr. That is still a strong balance sheet, but it is no longer a cash story.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean accounts and strong cash, but the parent takes its share first

bullets: **Cash backs profit.** Operating cash flow was 135% of net profit in FY26 and 77% in FY25 (working capital and taxes); over FY21-FY26 it averaged well above 100% because suppliers fund inventory.

**Royalty.** HMIL paid HMC ₹1,975 cr in FY26 (₹1,878 cr in FY25), ~2.8% of revenue and ~21% of pre-royalty profit before tax. It rises with sales; its terms (rate base, duration) are not disclosed in the annual report.

**Related-party purchases.** ~₹15,740 cr (30% of purchases) came from group companies (Mobis India alone ₹8,733 cr). Prices are said to be at arm's length and are approved by shareholders, but outsiders cannot test them.

**Incentives in revenue.** ₹1,372 cr of export and state incentives (duty drawback, RoDTEP, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra schemes) sit in operating revenue: real cash, but policy-dependent (~16% of FY26 EBITDA).
**Other income** is mostly interest on deposits (₹547 cr) plus exchange gains (₹133 cr in FY26) that we do not forecast.

**Contingent liabilities.** CCI penalty of ₹420.3 cr (spare parts / dealer practices; enforcement subject to a Madras High Court writ appeal) and a separate ₹87 cr CCI penalty under appeal; GST compensation-cess demand of ₹258.7 cr plus an equal penalty on certain SUVs (stayed by the Madras High Court); excise demand of ₹357.4 cr plus an equal penalty; draft income-tax assessments of ₹172.9 cr pending before the DRP. None is provided for; all are under appeal.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Unqualified audit by BSR & Co. LLP, a simple balance sheet, net cash and no aggressive capitalisation visible. The watch items are governance, not accounting: the royalty, related-party purchases and old regulatory disputes.

sections.title: Net cash of ~₹9,500 cr, negative working capital and a new ₹7,000 cr plant

blocks.p: At Mar-2026 Hyundai held ₹10,552 cr of cash and bank deposits against ₹1,098 cr of borrowings (mainly a Tamil Nadu sales-tax soft loan and leases): ~₹9,450 cr net, ~₹116 a share. Net fixed assets almost doubled to ₹13,070 cr after the Pune (Talegaon) plant, acquired from General Motors in Aug-2023 and re-equipped for ₹6,986 cr, was capitalised; CWIP fell from ₹4,718 cr to ₹725 cr. Other current financial assets (₹663 cr) are mainly incentives due from the Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra governments. Contingent liabilities are material but old: a ₹420 cr Competition Commission penalty under appeal, tax and duty demands (GST cess ₹259 cr plus an equal penalty, stayed by the Madras High Court).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Hyundai Motor India (consolidated, Rs crore; subsidiaries are tiny: an engineering-services company and an insurance broker). Revenue = vehicles sold (domestic + exports, company wholesale basis) x revenue per vehicle (all operating revenue incl. parts, engineering services, export incentives and government scheme income, divided by vehicles). The domestic / export build is in `build` and is checked against model revenue in tools/authoring/HYUNDAI.ctx.js. FY26 base: 775,031 vehicles (584,906 domestic + 190,125 exports), revenue Rs70,763 cr, Rs913,033 per vehicle. Screener's Net Profit equals Profit for EPS (no minorities), so no patchRaw. Shares 81.25 cr (IPO in Oct-2024 was a pure offer for sale: no new shares). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS as the street does.

volume._why: Company wholesale volumes (domestic + exports). FY27E 827,673 (+6.8%): domestic +9% (guidance 8-10%; Apr-Aug +12.6% to 247,980; Sep-Mar must grow ~7% against the GST-boosted base, helped by the Bayon mid-SUV from Oct-2026, the localised compact EV in H2 and the Pune third shift from Oct-2026; management expects the industry to grow only in low single digits in H2) and exports flat at 190,125 (guidance 8-10%, but Apr-Aug was -11.7%: Q1 -19.6% on the West Asia conflict and the June supplier fire, July +31%, August -31% on shipping constraints). FY28E +9.9% (domestic +10%: full year of two new nameplates, Chennai Plant 1 utilisation 72% to ~90% in CY27, Pune Phase 2 by CY28; exports +10% from a low base: new Venue global sourcing, Exter LHD, Verna PE, EV and Bayon exports). FY29E +8% (both). Capacity 994k at Mar-26 (Chennai 824k + Pune 170k), 1.07 mn after Pune Phase 2 (CY28), >1.1 mn by 2030: FY29E volume is ~92% of the CY28 capacity. Brokers: MOSL ~9% volume CAGR FY26-28E; Nirmal Bang 9.3%; JM domestic 8.5%/8.2%, exports 10%/12%.

assumptions._revPerUnitWhy: Revenue per vehicle = revenue from operations / wholesale volume: Rs897,690 (FY24), Rs907,982 (FY25), Rs913,038 (FY26); Q1FY27 Rs917,251 (+0.8% YoY, +2.1% QoQ; JM). FY27E +2.5%: three price rises in CY26 (~100bp cumulative), lower discounts (2.8% of ASP in Q1FY27 vs 3.4%), Bayon (above Venue) and the EV (priced above ICE equivalents) in H2, rupee weakness on export ASPs (export ASP +7% YoY in Q1). FY28E +3%: full-year mix of two new SUVs and the EV. FY29E +2.5%: price ~1.5% plus mix. Parts revenue fell in FY26 (Rs3,392 cr vs Rs4,306 cr) and is a drag we do not try to forecast separately.
assumptions._marginWhy: EBITDA margin (Screener basis, before other income): 12.5% FY23, 13.0% FY24, 12.9% FY25, 12.1% FY26, 9.3% in Q1FY27 (supplier fire cost ~13,900 vehicles, mostly Creta; exports -20%; commodity hit ~100bp QoQ and ~200bp YoY in precious metals and copper; Pune stabilisation costs; employee cost +20%). Guidance: 11-14% for FY27, reiterated on 30-Jul-2026. FY27E 11.0% = Q1 9.3% plus ~11.5% for Q2-Q4 (volume recovery, price rises, no launch discounts on new models) - the bottom of the range, because commodity pressure is not over and the EV and Bayon launches carry marketing and start-up costs. FY28E 12.3%: Chennai Plant 1 utilisation back to ~90%, operating leverage on the Pune plant, localisation 83% to 90% by 2030. FY29E 12.8%, still below FY24-25 (~13%): royalty (2.8% of revenue), EV mix and competition (M&M, Tata, Maruti, Kia in SUVs). Street FY27E 11.0% (Nirmal Bang) to 12.1% (BOB Caps); FY28E 11.4% to 13.3%; Nomura 11.5% / 12.7% / 13.4%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY27 capex guided at ~Rs7,500 cr, 'the highest ever' (Q4FY26 call, 8-May-2026): mainly Pune Phase 2 (170k to 250k by CY28) and Chennai upgrades, plus the two FY27 launches. The company plans to invest Rs45,000 cr over FY26-FY30 in capacity, electrification and 26 new products and variants (AR FY26); Screener capex FY26 Rs4,266 cr. Pune Phase 3 (+70k to ~320k by 2030) follows. We model Rs8,500 cr a year for FY28-29E; spending the full Rs45,000 cr plan would mean ~Rs11,000 cr a year in FY28-30, a downside risk to free cash flow.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs2,198 cr = 7.7% of average gross block (Rs28,692 cr), but gross block jumped by Rs7,997 cr when the Pune plant was capitalised in H2FY26. Q1FY27 depreciation Rs557 cr (Rs2,228 cr annualised). The engine holds CWIP flat (Rs725 cr) and depreciates capex at once, although much of the Rs7,500-8,500 cr a year will sit in CWIP until Pune Phase 2 starts; 6.2% gives Rs2,259 cr in FY27E, Rs2,755 cr in FY28E and Rs3,282 cr in FY29E (3.4% of revenue vs 3.0-3.2% in FY24-26).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Treasury = cash and bank deposits (Rs10,552 cr at Mar-26) less borrowings (Rs1,098 cr incl. leases) = Rs9,461 cr. FY26 interest income Rs547 cr (fixed deposits Rs455 cr, tax refunds Rs14 cr, others Rs76 cr; AR FY26 consolidated note 30) on average gross cash of Rs9,566 cr = 5.7%; on average net cash (~Rs8,600 cr) ~6.4%. FY25: Rs616 cr. Deposit rates fell in 2025-26, so 5.8% on net treasury.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: royalty received Rs120 cr (FY26), rental income Rs49 cr, other non-operating income Rs92 cr and profit on asset sales Rs7 cr = ~Rs270 cr in FY26, growing with the business; plus a small allowance for exchange gains. FY26 reported other income Rs949 cr (AR note 30) = interest Rs547 cr + royalty Rs120 cr + exchange gain Rs133 cr + rental Rs49 cr + other Rs100 cr; Screener shows Rs986 cr (including Rs4 cr of exceptional items and classification differences). TTM to Jun-26 Rs1,001 cr. We do not forecast most exchange gains (Rs133 cr in FY26, Rs13 cr in FY25), so FY27E other income (~Rs800 cr) is below FY26.
assumptions._interestLabel: Interest cost (SIPCOT soft loan, leases, working-capital lines)
assumptions._interestWhy: FY26 Rs106 cr; Q1FY27 Rs27 cr. Borrowings Rs1,098 cr at Mar-26 (long-term Rs455 cr, mainly the Tamil Nadu sales-tax soft loan; short-term Rs542 cr; leases Rs101 cr), repaid over time.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective tax 25.9% in FY25 and FY26 (statutory 25.17% plus disallowances such as CSR); Q1FY27 26.0%.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend Rs21 a share for FY25 and FY26 (30% and 31.4% of EPS). The revised dividend policy (Oct-2025) sets no fixed payout. FY24 included ~Rs15,400 cr of dividends paid to HMC before the IPO (derived from the fall in reserves), which we do not expect to repeat while capex is Rs7,500-8,500 cr a year.

Revenue per vehicle is one blended figure; the split of revenue by geography (AR FY26 note 29: domestic vehicles Rs45,150 cr, exported vehicles Rs15,598 cr; parts Rs3,392 cr; services Rs5,251 cr; other operating revenue Rs1,372 cr) is shown in the report but not modelled separately.
